changes.before: A model is excellent on its training photos but poor on new photos. Which conclusion is justified?
changes.after: Doing well on training examples does not prove a model handles new ones.

before: Generalization means applying what was learned to new examples from the intended kind of task.
Overfitting happens when a model fits training details too closely and performs worse on new examples.
A bird model might rely on a familiar background instead of the bird. It can succeed on practice photos and fail elsewhere.
Compare training results with separate validation results. Excellent training performance alone is not enough.
New conditions can also differ from all earlier data. A model trained only on daylight photos needs evaluation before being trusted at night.
after: Generalization means using a learned pattern successfully on new examples of the intended task.
Overfitting happens when a model learns details of its training examples that do not help enough on new examples.
The bird model might have learned a background that appeared often in training. Check its mistakes and the data before deciding what went wrong.

Validation photos should match the task you care about. If this model must work at night, include suitable night photos in its evaluation. Success on daylight photos alone does not show that it can do this.

before.question: A model is excellent on its training photos but poor on new photos. Which conclusion is justified?
choices: Training success proves the new photos were all mislabeled.
A perfect training score guarantees useful performance everywhere.
Training success alone has not established generalization.
before.explanation: Separate examples test whether the useful behavior extends beyond the training set.

after.question: A model does well on training photos but poorly on new photos. What can you conclude?
choices: All new photos must have wrong labels.
The training score proves it works everywhere.
The training score alone does not show that it handles new photos well.
after.explanation: Separate examples show whether the useful pattern carries over beyond training.

changes.before: Concept-only lesson. No programming, API key, model execution, or account connection is required. Sources support general concepts, not claims about private model internals.
changes.after: The code visual is a small teaching example. You do not need to write code, connect an AI account, or use an API key.

project.title: Learning a useful pattern, not just the examples
project.task: Explain what a high training score does and does not show.
